I looked at the project and the current MCP documentation. Your storybook does **not** use MCP events. It uses Deepgram speech events: `StartOfTurn` tells it a child has begun speaking, and `EndOfTurn` provides the finished words. The interruption change uses `StartOfTurn` to stop the narrator. [Deepgram event handling](/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/interactive-storybook/lib/audio/client.ts:187)

In MCP, “events” usually means **notifications about changes or progress** between an MCP server and client. They would not make this microphone reaction faster on their own. [MCP specification update](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/)

content.text:
You’re right. I looked up **MCP Events**, the new specification, and I had confused it with ordinary MCP notifications. Sorry.

MCP Events lets an MCP server tell an AI agent that something happened **without waiting for a user to ask**. For example, a connected service could report “a new story was saved,” and an agent could then start a task. Clients can receive events by polling, an open stream, or a webhook. The specification is currently a **beta extension**, and both the server and client must support it. [Official MCP Events overview](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/events/overview)

For your storybook, it could be useful for **background work**—say, an agent reacting when a saved adventure is ready for review. It would not be the right mechanism for stopping the narrator when a child speaks; that immediate interaction already runs through Deepgram’s live speech events. This is my assessment of where the spec fits your app, not a claim made by the spec.
im trying to figure out how i would incorporate something like that..or maybe it wouldnt make sense because there's no mcp server here

Yes—your instinct is right. **MCP Events only makes sense if your storybook needs to notify an external AI agent**. You would add an MCP server that publishes events, and an MCP client would subscribe to them. The [spec describes that server–client flow](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/events/overview).

For example, an event could say “a child saved an adventure,” letting a separate agent prepare a parent summary. Your current story experience does not need that extra layer. The browser already receives the child’s speech through a live Deepgram connection, which is the right place to handle narrator interruptions.

My suggestion: **don’t add MCP Events for now**. Consider it if you later want ChatGPT or another external agent to react to activity in the storybook while nobody is using the app.
im trying to figure out a use case for an external agent

The strongest use case I see is a **parent’s story companion**.

When a child finishes and saves an adventure, your storybook could send an MCP Event to an external agent. The agent could prepare a short note for the parent: what the child invented, which characters they liked, and an idea for continuing the story together. The parent would choose whether to use it.

That gives the external agent a clear job **outside the live storytelling session**. It can react after a story is saved, while the child’s conversation stays fast and focused.

I’d only build this if you want the storybook to connect to an agent the parent already uses, such as ChatGPT. If the recap would appear only inside your own app, a normal background job would be simpler than an MCP server.
